Profile a representative warmed-up interval with CPU and CUDA activities, shapes/stacks only when needed, and explicit ranges for loading, transfer, forward, backward, and optimizer steps. Use a system timeline for kernel launches, memory copies, synchronization, and distributed communication; avoid measuring only asynchronous Python launch time. [1](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/index.html) [2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-c-programming-guide/)

Long GPU idle gaps between kernels with busy Python or delayed input delivery suggest CPU/loader starvation; correlate them with data-ready timestamps. Long NCCL kernels or waits around collectives suggest communication or rank imbalance, but a slow compute rank can make other ranks appear communication-bound. Inspect all ranks, overlap, transfer bandwidth, and batch sizes. Fix the measured bottleneck, rerun the same workload, and report throughput plus tail latency rather than optimizing an isolated kernel unrelated to the critical path.
